messages.subject: Poisson HMM - convergence/autocorrelation issues
parts:
Hey all, 

I've been using NIMBLE to implement a discrete-time Poisson Hidden Markov Model, but am having convergence issues with the lambda parameters. I have tried RW, conjugate, and blocking samplers for these parameters, both a poisson and zero inflated poisson distribution for the data, thinning, as well as some fist shaking at the computer. Any help/further suggestions would be greatly appreciated. 

I'm including a brief model overview below, and have attached NIMBLE code and simulated latent state values for reproducibility. In the code I am holding the latent states as constants to try and isolate the issues with the lambda convergence, but ultimately these will be estimated as well. 

Cheers, 
Meridith 

2-state Penalized HMM Model  (see attached for NIMBLE model code)

Observed Data: 
Y_t ~ Poisson(lambda_{X_t})

Augmented Data Scheme:
Y_t = Y_Low + Y_Diff * I{X_t = H}

Y_L ~ Pois(lambda_{X_t = L})
Y_Diff ~ Pois(lambda_{X_t = H})

Lambda Priors:
lambda_{X_t = L} ~ Gamma(shape = .005, rate = .7)
lambda_{X_t = H} ~ Gamma(shape = .05, rate = .7)

Latent States: 
X_t ~ Mult(1, P_{X_{t-1}}) (Bernulloi in commented out code due to 2-states, but generalized to Mult)

Probability Transition Matrix Priors
 P[i, ] ~ Dirch(alpha = theta[i, ] )


where theta provides a penalty tuning parameter.

theta = [tau, 1
              1, tau]

where a larger tau value places more weight on staying in a latent state for a longer period of time before switching (i.e. from Low to High or vic versa).

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Poisson HMM - convergence/autocorrelation issues
parts:
I'm not seeing where there are data values to inform any parameters.

It looks like both y_l and y_diff are not given as data, so they are being sampled as well.  In effect it looks like lambda_l will follow its prior but in a slow way because of the many y_l[t]'s also being sampled as if they are posterior predictive nodes.  You could use monitors2 and thin2 to get a thinner sample of y_l and y_diff and try to understand what is happening.  I think it is an mcmc phenomenon, not a nimble problem.

When I do model$setData('y_l') after the model$simulate(c("y_l", "y_diff"), then y_l is now data and I get a sensible well-mixed posterior for lambda_l centered around its correct (simulation) value of 0.007.  I did not do a similar experiment with y_diff and lambda_diff.

HTH.
-Perry

messages.author: a7799393a04672fe
messages.subject: Re: Poisson HMM - convergence/autocorrelation issues
parts:
Thanks Perry!

I've added 

simulatedData <- model$y
model$setData(list(y = simulatedData))

to the code.

The separated y_l and y_diff aren't separately known when the latent state is high (1), only the combined y for each t. In this case using a multinomial distribution, the data, y, may be separated into y_l and y_diff to correspond with the two lambda parameters. 

However, when the latent state is low (0) then we want to constrict y_l = y and y_diff =  0. This is hard to code in Nimble where if/then statements aren't available for these parameters. 

In previous non-Nimble code this was accomplished via the following: 

for (t in 1:seconds) {
  if (state[t] == 0) {
    y_l[t] <- y[t]   
    y_diff[t] <- 0
  } else {
    split <- rmultinom(1, 
                       size = y[t], 
                       prob = c(lambda_l,
                                lambda_diff))
    y_l[t] <- split[1]
    y_diff[t] <- split[2]
  }
}

but I'm unable to figure out how to code this clearly in Nimble. Would a user-defined function be useful here? 
 
Thanks so much!
Meridith

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Poisson HMM - convergence/autocorrelation issues
parts:
Hi Meredith,

NIMBLE, along with JAGS and WinBUGS/OpenBUGS, uses a declarative model language.  That mean none of them will support the if-then structure you have or the re-use of split in the style of iterative (typical) programming. In other words, you can't re-use split for each t, because once it is declared it is part of the graph as declared, so you will need to index it by t.  Also model declarations need indexing. It is also not clear if you are trying to have a variable follow a multinomial (dmultinom) or to draw from a multinomial (rmultinom) in a nimbleFunction outside of a model, because it is not typical for an "r" function to appear in model code.  So, I can't really tell what you're trying to do.  If you are trying to write model code, and if I guess at your intention, it might be something like this:

nimbleCode({
for(t in 1:seconds) {
  split[t, 1:2] ~ dmultinom(size = y[t], 
                                 prob = c(lambda_l,
                                               lambda_diff))
  y_l[t] <- (state[t] == 0) * y[t] + (state[t] != 0) * split[t, 1]
  y_diff[t] <- (state[t] != 0) * split[t, 2]
})

HTH
-Perry
